articles.title: Foxglove Heights Elementary Board Approves Playground Upgrade
articles.deck: The program begins in March and is open to all students in grade 4 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for March. Principal Agnes Weatherby said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the winter term.
Students will meet on Tuesday afternoons in the Kettle Hill Park gate, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.

articles.title: Eastgate Garden Club Adds Street Tree Planting
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 33 weeks and will be paid for with $7,500 raised locally.
body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Foundry Row fire house on Monday at 7 p.m. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings.

The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The effort began in July when a handful of neighbors met at the Foundry Row fire house to talk about street tree planting.

Ida Mahoney, who has lived on Prospect Terrace for 33 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Several residents on Prospect Terrace said they had been waiting since 1988 for something like this.

articles.title: Nora Hartigan, 73, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Nora Hartigan for the many years of service to Kettle Hill.
body: Born in Kettle Hill in the years after the war, Nora Hartigan spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Kettle Hill.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Canal Park Food Pantry in his or her name. Nora Hartigan died in September at home on Warren Avenue, at the age of 73.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to St. Brendan’s Parish
body: To the editor: Please keep the book exchange box in the budget. Many of us on Yardley Avenue use it every week. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

To the editor: I have lived on Yardley Avenue for 22 years, and I want to say what a difference St. Brendan’s Parish has made. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the May meeting.
Agnes Mahoney, Lower Millrace

articles.title: Tannery Flats Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 4 residents spoke at Tuesday’s session.
body: Councilmember Simone Dunmore asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $1,200. Residents of Tannery Flats said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Public works estimates the work will take about 4 weeks once it starts in July. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
